subject: P1 text first (radar echo tops behind --storm-layers): uncommitted working tree on top of HEAD b0c4274; website, tests and workflow identical to commit 1916091
verdict: Do not ship as-is. One blocking evidence-honesty defect: an echo top is stated without the no-data heights above it. Otherwise the flag-off build is byte-identical to HEAD, the live storm build passes browser checks at 288, 390 and 1440 px, and the remaining items are fixable in small steps.

blocking.what: The echo top is stated as the top even when heights above it had no radar data. column() (lines 205-207) takes the highest height with 35 dBZ among heights that have data; _describe() (228-230) then writes 'Echo top (radar estimate): N m above sea level' with no qualifier, and the no-data count appears only in brackets. Reproduced through the real _results() with 40 dBZ at 1, 2 and 3 km, no radar data at 4-15 km, ground 975.1 m: 'Echo top (radar estimate): 3,000 m above sea level ... dBZ 35 or more at 3 of the 3 sampled heights with radar data above ground (7 with no radar data; 1 below ground, not used). This is not an all-clear.' The same unqualified 'highest of 11 heights' claim is in map.html:195, town.html:81, about.html:25 and sources.py:136-138. Radar data above 6 km is scarce in the real files: at 2026-10-17 09:00:36 UTC the CONUS grid had 3.3% valid dBZ at 6 km, 0.5% at 10 km and 0.1% at 15 km (computed with pygrib from the 11 downloaded files); mrms.json records -99 at 100% of Montana cells at 10 km (02:04:39 UTC). A storm topping at 3 km can therefore read as a 3 km top. 'No echo' (storm.py:224-226) has the same gap: 'No echo at or above 35 dBZ ... at the 1 sampled heights' is stated from one height when 10 were no-data.
blocking.fix: In column() count and list the heights above the top with no radar data. In _describe(), when that count is above 0, say 'at least N m above sea level' or 'the top may be higher: K heights above it had no radar data', never the bare sentence. For 'No echo' with few data heights, say 'only D of A heights above ground had radar data'. Change the List, town-page, About and CONTRACTS sentences from 'the highest of 11 heights' to 'the highest sampled height with 35 dBZ, among heights that had radar data'. Add tests: 40 dBZ at 1-3 km with no data above (assert the qualifier, and that '3,000 m' never appears unqualified) and one sparse 'No echo' case. No test covers a top with no-data heights above it; the EchoTop tests use Billings, where every height above the top has data.

should_fix.what: New browser script (37 lines, 1,741 B). It adds a JavaScript duty that is not in research/globe/README.md section 9b's 'complete list' (lines 469-492) and has no line or byte cap (caps table, lines 494-501; section 6: 'a line and byte limit for each browser file'). The plan says new JavaScript duties need Carson's ruling (section 2, D-G1; docs/ROADMAP.md lines 61-66, Next 9). The header comment (lines 1-4) gives a browser-only reason, which is defensible: it places text into sheets that map.js builds at run time, and a separate file avoids growing map.js (no-growth cap). No Python test exercises it: removing its guard (line 18) survives every test (mutant js-guard-off).
should_fix.fix: Either add the duty to section 9b with a row and a line and byte cap test (as layers.js has), or get Carson's ruling first. The flag already keeps it off main.

should_fix.what: decode_level() indexes msg.values, and _no_data_to_nan() then calls np.asarray(..., float64), which ignores a masked array's mask. gridded.py applies np.ma.filled(..., np.nan) (gridded.py:195 and :477). Real pygrib 2.1.8 returned a plain float64 ndarray for these 11 files (bitmapPresent 0), so the gap is latent: a masked cell would read its underlying number, possibly a large value, as an echo. No test uses a masked array.
should_fix.fix: picked = np.ma.filled(np.ma.asarray(values[rows, cols], dtype=np.float64), np.nan), before the del. Add a unit test with a masked cell holding 40.0 and expect NaN.

should_fix.what: Mutation check on scratch copies (18 mutants; the storm test classes plus Contracts and SampleBuild; the repo was not edited): 12 killed, 6 survived. Survivors: threshold 35 -> 40 (storm.py:205); strict 'dBZ > 35' (storm.py:205); at-ground boundary '> ground' (storm.py:203); workflow flag removed from the branch line (website.yml:95); storm.js guard removed (storm.js:18); sample weak echo written as 0 dBZ (sample.py). No test covers the 35 dBZ boundary (34.9, 35.0, 39.9), a level exactly at ground, or the workflow build lines (tests/test_website_workflow.py has no storm check). tools/smoke_map.py has no storm check, so branch previews do not test the new sheets.
should_fix.fix: Add boundary tests in EchoTop (34.9, 35.0, 39.9 at a height with data; level equal to ground). Add a workflow test: the main build line has no --storm-layers, the branch line has it, and tests.test_storm is in the unittest line. Add to tools/smoke_map.py: the List has 14 storm items; each town sheet has one storm block with its own text before 'Official alerts'; still one after Back. The review ran this check and it passed (verified_ok).

should_fix.what: Owner-facing wording depends on an open question. Live build at 2026-10-17 09:28:42 UTC: all 11 heights sentinel-coded in all 14 towns, so every town reads 'No radar data (radar estimate) at any of the N sampled heights above ground'; the status detail says 'no radar data above ground at 14 of 14'. The P0 record (research/globe/validation-evidence/p0-gates.json, gate_status) says the -99/-999 meaning is 'not settled' and keeps 'No radar data' under D-G13. The real 09:00:36 UTC files show -999 at 92.8% of CONUS cells at 0.5 km and -99 at 66.3% at 15 km, a pattern that could also mean clear air at low levels. README section 6 lists the NSSL check as a P0 done-when, and P1 is product code, which P0 forbids ('Gates; no product code').
should_fix.fix: Keep the text off main (it is). Tell the owner that quiet weather will show 'No radar data' for every town. If the meaning stays open, name both codes without a cause, for example 'no radar value (-99 or -999; meaning not verified)'. Record in ROADMAP that P1 was built ahead of the NSSL check.

should_fix.what: CONTRACTS storm_levels 'missing' (lines 141-144) omits the ground-height rule: a town whose NWS grid height did not load gets 'Echo top not available', never a value. The ground height is the NWS gridpoint elevation (sources.py:427 converts metres to feet; build.py:221 divides by M_TO_FT = 3.280840, sources.py:30, giving metres back). The plan's terrain source is USGS 3DEP (README section 3, 'Terrain (PG2)'; research/globe/validation-evidence/terrain.json gives Billings 951.9-953.4 m). The live NWS grid value for Billings is 975.1 m, 22 m higher. Below-ground counts use this value (storm.py:203).
should_fix.fix: Add the ground-height rule and the source difference to the contract's units or missing text. Decide with the owner whether the NWS grid-square elevation (a value for a grid of about 2.5 km) stays for P1.
